description:
Design a 16-bit ALU that performs the following operations based on a 4-bit operation code (opcode):
- 0000: ADD
- 0001: SUBTRACT
- 0010: AND
- 0011: OR
- 0100: XOR
The ALU should take two 16-bit inputs and output a 16-bit result.
code:
module ALU_16bit (
    input [15:0] A,
    input [15:0] B,
    input [3:0] opcode,
    output reg [15:0] result
);
    always @(*) begin
        case (opcode)
            4'b0000: result = A + B;         // ADD
            4'b0001: result = A - B;         // SUBTRACT
            4'b0010: result = A & B;         // AND
            4'b0011: result = A | B;         // OR
            4'b0100: result = A ^ B;         // XOR
            default: result = 16'b0;         // Default case
        endcase
    end
endmodule

Design a Stop-and-Wait protocol for a simple communication system where a sender sends data one packet at a time and waits for an acknowledgment from the receiver before sending the next packet. The sender should have a state to indicate whether it is waiting for acknowledgment or sending data. The system should also include a simple clock and reset mechanism to control the timing of the operations.
code:
module stop_and_wait (
    input clk,
    input reset,
    input send_data,
    input ack,
    output reg data_out,
    output reg state // 0 = waiting, 1 = sending
);
    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            state <= 0;
            data_out <= 0;
        end else begin
            case (state)
                0: begin // waiting state
                    if (send_data) begin
                        data_out <= 1; // send data
                        state <= 1; // move to sending state
                    end
                end
                1: begin // sending state
                    if (ack) begin
                        data_out <= 0; // clear data output
                        state <= 0; // move back to waiting state
                    end
                end
            endcase
        end
    end
endmodule

Design an SPI Master Controller in Verilog that can transmit data to an SPI slave device. The controller should provide the following functionality:
1. Generate SPI clock (SCK).
2. Shift out a byte of data on MOSI while keeping MISO in a high-impedance state.
3. Control Chip Select (CS) signal to indicate the start and end of communication.
4. The controller should be able to handle a simple transmit operation triggered by an external start signal.
code:
module spi_master (
    input wire clk,          // System clock
    input wire reset,        // Reset signal
    input wire start,        // Start transmission signal
    input wire [7:0] data_in,// Data to be transmitted
    output reg mosi,         // Master Out Slave In
    output reg sck,          // SPI Clock
    output reg cs,           // Chip Select
    output reg busy          // Busy signal
);
    reg [2:0] state;         // State register
    reg [2:0] bit_counter;   // Bit counter for shifting
    reg [7:0] shift_reg;     // Shift register

    localparam IDLE = 3'b000, START = 3'b001, SHIFT = 3'b010, STOP = 3'b011;

    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            state <= IDLE;
            mosi <= 1'bz; // High impedance
            sck <= 0;
            cs <= 1; // CS inactive
            busy <= 0;
            bit_counter <= 0;
        end else begin
            case (state)
                IDLE: begin
                    if (start) begin
                        cs <= 0; // Activate CS
                        shift_reg <= data_in; // Load data into shift register
                        busy <= 1;
                        bit_counter <= 0;
                        state <= START;
                    end
                end
                START: begin
                    sck <= 0; // Start with SCK low
                    state <= SHIFT;
                end
                SHIFT: begin
                    if (bit_counter < 8) begin
                        mosi <= shift_reg[7]; // Output MSB first
                        shift_reg <= {shift_reg[6:0], 1'b0}; // Shift left
                        sck <= ~sck; // Toggle SCK
                        if (sck) begin
                            bit_counter <= bit_counter + 1; // Increment bit counter
                        end
                    end else begin
                        state <= STOP; // If all bits are shifted
                    end
                end
                STOP: begin
                    sck <= 0; // Ensure SCK is low
                    cs <= 1; // Deactivate CS
                    busy <= 0;
                    state <= IDLE; // Return to idle
                end
            endcase
        end
    end
endmodule

description: Design a Booth multiplier in Verilog that takes two n-bit signed binary numbers as inputs and produces their product as a result. The design should handle negative numbers using two's complement representation and produce an output that is twice the bit-width of the input numbers.
code:
module booth_multiplier (
    input signed [n-1:0] A,
    input signed [n-1:0] B,
    output reg signed [2*n-1:0] P
);
    parameter n = 4; // You can change this parameter for different bit widths
    reg signed [2*n-1:0] M;
    reg signed [n-1:0] Q;
    reg Qn;
    reg signed [2*n-1:0] A_temp;
    integer i;

    always @(*) begin
        M = A; // Multiplicand
        Q = B; // Multiplier
        Qn = 0; // Qn starts as 0
        P = 0; // Clear product

        for (i = 0; i < n; i = i + 1) begin
            if (Q[0] == 1 && Qn == 0) begin
                P = P + M; // Add M to the product
            end else if (Q[0] == 0 && Qn == 1) begin
                P = P - M; // Subtract M from the product
            end

            Qn = Q[0]; // Store Qn
            P = P >> 1; // Arithmetic right shift P
            Q = {P[2*n-1], Q}; // Extend Q with the sign bit of P
        end
    end
endmodule

Design a Verilog module that implements the Bellman-Ford algorithm to compute the shortest path from a source node to all other nodes in a directed graph. The graph is represented as an adjacency matrix, and the weight of edges can be positive or negative. The module should take the number of nodes and the adjacency matrix as inputs, along with a source node, and output the shortest distance from the source to each node.
code:
module bellman_ford #(parameter N = 5) (
    input wire clk,
    input wire rst,
    input wire [N*N-1:0] adj_matrix, // adjacency matrix
    input wire [N-1:0] weights,        // weights of edges
    input wire [2:0] source,           // source node
    output reg [N-1:0] distance        // shortest distances
);
    integer i, j, k;
    reg [N-1:0] dist [0:N-1]; // distance array

    always @(posedge clk or posedge rst) begin
        if (rst) begin
            for (i = 0; i < N; i = i + 1) begin
                dist[i] = (i == source) ? 0 : 8'd255; // Initialize distances
            end
        end else begin
            for (k = 0; k < N-1; k = k + 1) begin
                for (i = 0; i < N; i = i + 1) begin
                    for (j = 0; j < N; j = j + 1) begin
                        if (adj_matrix[i*N+j] && dist[i] + weights[i*N+j] < dist[j]) begin
                            dist[j] = dist[i] + weights[i*N+j];

    localparam TRANSMITTING = 2'b01;
    localparam COMPLETED = 2'b10;

            end

            end

        endcase
    end

The data and response should be valid for one clock cycle. Control signals include `clk`, `start`, `MOSI`, `MISO`, and `CS` (chip select). The master should generate the clock and control the chip select for data transmission.
code:
module spi_master (
    input wire clk,
    input wire start,
    input wire [3:0] data_in,
    output reg [3:0] data_out,
    output reg MOSI,
    input wire MISO,
    output reg CS
);
    reg [2:0] state;
    reg [1:0] bit_count;
    reg [3:0] shift_reg;

    localparam IDLE = 3'b000,
               SEND = 3'b001,
               RECEIVE = 3'b010,
               DONE = 3'b011;

    always @(posedge clk) begin
        case (state)
            IDLE: begin
                CS <= 1;  // Deassert chip select
                if (start) begin
                    CS <= 0;  // Assert chip select
                    shift_reg <= data_in; // Load data
                    bit_count <= 0;
                    state <= SEND;
                end
            end

            SEND: begin
                if (bit_count < 4) begin
                    MOSI <= shift_reg[3]; // Send MSB first
                    shift_reg <= {shift_reg[2:0], 1'b0}; // Shift left
                    bit_count <= bit_count + 1;
                end else begin
                    state <= RECEIVE;
                    bit_count <= 0;
                end
            end

            RECEIVE: begin
                if (bit_count < 4) begin
                    data_out[3] <= MISO; // Receive MSB first
                    data_out <= {data_out[2:0], 1'b0}; // Shift left
                    bit_count <= bit_count + 1;
                end else begin
                    state <= DONE;
                    CS <= 1; // Deassert chip select
                end
            end

            DONE: begin
                state <= IDLE; // Return to idle state
            end

            default: state <= IDLE;
        endcase
    end
endmodule

            case (last_granted)
